language_context.national_language_note: Japanese is the predominant language of public life. The country's linguistic landscape also includes Indigenous Ainu and Ryukyuan languages, as well as regional varieties and community languages.
language_context.diversity_note: UNESCO's endangered-language references for Japan include Ainu and several Ryukyuan varieties, as well as Hachijo. Linguistic classification is contested in some cases; LWT records community and scholarly distinctions instead of automatically labelling all varieties as mere dialects.
language_context.documentation_unit: Use individual language/community profiles. Keep Japanese regional dialects distinct from separate Ryukyuan languages where the cited linguistic source does so.
